A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Self-Introspective Decoding (SID). All 32 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SID evaluations on POPE, CHAIR, GPT-assisted assessments, efficiency measurements, and ablations, alongside some baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains original SID experiments and reports additional MME/MMBench evaluations and DoLa comparisons.

M1.justification: SID still scores vision tokens using attention, preserves the least important tokens after early decoder layers, and contrastively subtracts the resulting logits. CT2S, its default pruning settings, and the decoding equations remain unchanged. Proposed future extensions are not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds MME and MMBench evaluations on LLaVA-1.5 7B, extending coverage from hallucination detection and image descriptions to broader perceptual and cognitive abilities. The original POPE datasets, MSCOCO captioning, Visual Genome evaluations, and LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild cases remain.

E2.justification: DoLa moves from related-work discussion to actual evaluation in the CHAIR and POPE comparisons. Its rows replace standalone Beam Search rows across the four backbones; OPERA remains. The other comparators in these experiments and the GPT-assisted comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New MME/MMBench evaluations use LLaVA-1.5 7B, with greedy decoding specified for SID, ICD, and VCD. Appendix A.2 specifies the new DoLa configuration. v2 also identifies LLaVA-NeXT as 8B rather than v1's blanket 7B description, although its appendix retains 7B wording; an actual backbone replacement is not established. Existing sample counts and generation budgets remain.

E4.justification: The analysis testing how token selection and input disturbances affect hallucinations receives a limited numerical revision: visual disturbance's CHAIRs changes from 52.7 to 56.7 in v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table 8. The layer/ratio, high/random-token, hyperparameter, larger-backbone, alternate-decoding, and case-study analyses are otherwise retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same uncertainty entries and three-run averaging statement. The larger-backbone table likewise retains three-run averaging. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds evidence on general multimodal ability: Table 5 reports SID scores of 1520.2 on MME and 65.1 on MMBench, without v1 counterparts. It also adds DoLa results and removes Beam Search entries. The visual-disturbance CHAIRs value changes from 52.7 to 56.7, and the GPT-4 radar display is revised. Matched SID scores in the main POPE and CHAIR tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content, including attention scoring, contrastive decoding, the additive alternative, and CHAIR definitions. Moving the metric definitions to Appendix A.3 adds no theory. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2's abstract explicitly claims hallucination reduction without compromising LVLMs' general ability, extending the earlier emphasis on faithful, high-quality text and efficiency. The central SID/CT2S contribution and the critique of holistic input disturbances remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets MME/MMBench results as preserving or improving general multimodal ability and acknowledges sampling's slight advantages in unigram fluency and words per image. Its new future-work discussion identifies manually chosen pruning layers/ratios and proposes learned selection and CT2S-generated negative instructions as possible extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds DoLa's candidate layers, mature layer, and repetition penalty. v2 adds an anonymous code-access link while retaining the GitHub link, but removes v1's dataset-access statement and direct dataset links. Its front-page statement that code is in the appendix is not fulfilled by the supplied appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including MME, MMBench, HallusionBench, RLHF-V, and DiffRate, while removing some application, counterfactual-bias, and scaling-law background references. SID's positioning as an efficient, training-free alternative to raw-input contrastive disturbances remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially condensed and rewritten. The method narrative is split into preliminary/motivation and methodology sections, while background, evaluation details, GPT4-V results, and several ablations move into organized appendix subsections. A future-work discussion is added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different layout with resized and wrapped displays and reorganized appendix figures. v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Table 2, a new benchmark table appears, and several charts are redrawn. The Shikra radar chart's SHR scale is corrected to make outward values lower, consistent with the stated metric direction.

improvement.justification: The added general-capability evaluations and actual DoLa comparisons modestly strengthen validation beyond v1's hallucination-focused evidence. Clearer organization, explicit manual-setting limitations, and the corrected Shikra SHR display also help. These benefits outweigh limited losses from removing standalone Beam Search controls and dataset-access links, although the inconsistent 7B/8B description remains. The new capability results cover only one backbone, so the overall gain is limited.
